In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the beta-adrenoceptors are heterogenous and consist of at least two different subtypes.
there are two classes of beta-adrenoceptor in rat liver membranes.
125I- and 3H-iodocyanpindolol bind to the same site, but the 3H-ligand also labels a second site which is not recognized by 125I- iodocyanopindlol.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the beta-adrenoceptors of rat liver can be divided into at least three classes of receptors, two beta 1 and one beta 2.
3H-dialprenolol binds to two classes of sites, one of which is not an alpha-adrenoceptor and which may not be a beta-adrenoceptor. 125I-Idocyanopindoliol binds to only one class of binding site.
3H-dialprenolol binds to beta-adrenoceptor sites and to a non-specific binding site. 125I-ICYP binds to beta-adrenergic sites only.
The main takeaway from our work is that
3H-dHA binding to rat liver membranes is not specific for beta-adrenergic receptors.
the binding characteristics of 125I- iodocyanopindoli are more suitable for the study of the beta-adrenergic receptor in rat liver than the binding characteristics of [3H]-dihydroalprenalol.
